says: In next/, E83 turned TomlParser's array-hole guard from Object.hasOwn(value, i) into Predicate.hasProperty(value, i), which is the in operator, so an array whose prototype chain holds that index (a custom or polluted prototype, or a Proxy) no longer throws 'A TOML array cannot contain a missing element', and value.map then writes the inherited value; no law reaches the guard.
proof: A probe on Node 26.13.0: an array [, 1] whose prototype holds 0 gives Object.hasOwn(arr, 0) false, 0 in arr true, and arr.map((v) => v) gives ["x",1]. In a scratch copy, replacing the guard's test with false leaves src/settings/TomlEdit.test.ts green, 18 of 18, and no test file names 'missing element'. A typed own-index form passes tsc --noEmit with libfabrika's tsconfig: const at = String(i); Predicate.hasProperty(value, at) && Rec.has<string, unknown>(value, at).
cost: Only odd arrays reach it today, but the file's own comment says own properties matter there, put and read beside it keep that rule, and a later edit that loosens the guard further goes unseen.

fix: Fixed in E83's fix round: the tests commit 50d3496b06b9e4e6f16923ede194dbc67bc2a07a adds the law to L5 in TomlEdit.test.ts, and the build commit 60b4241941418755aa2cbba35e898df8890e5797 checks own elements again through one owns helper in TomlParser.ts.
